original_question: Clarify the precise mathematical relationship between the infinite critical beta-splitting tree CTCS(infinity) and the beta(2,1) coalescent, including which structural correspondences are exact, which hold only asymptotically, and how the shared subordinator description should be interpreted.
target_in_paper: Section 5.3-5.5, especially Theorem 12, supported by Theorem 7 and Theorems 10-11: the exchangeable-partition formalization of CTCS(∞) and the exact subordinator law for the tagged clade-size process.
correct_elements: The draft correctly focuses on the infinite-limit object CTCS(∞), on the need to separate exact statements from asymptotic heuristics, and on the central role of the subordinator governing tagged clade sizes. It also correctly senses that the relevant issue is the relation between the finite-n trees and a limiting infinite object rather than a question about a single fixed CTCS(n).
missing_details: The paper does not mention or define a beta(2,1) coalescent, so making that the main comparison object is not paper-faithful and broadens beyond the paper’s stated results.

CTCS(∞) is not formalized in the paper as a locally finite infinite tree; instead it is formalized as an exchangeable partition process Π(t) of N obtained by cutting the consistent growth process at height t.
A stand-alone formulation must define Π(t), the ordered clades Π(t)_ℓ, the finite-n clade sizes K_{t,ℓ}^{(n)} := |Π(t)_ℓ ∩ [n]|, and the asymptotic frequencies P_{t,ℓ} := lim_{n→∞} K_{t,ℓ}^{(n)}/n.

The exact structural statement at fixed t is Kingman’s paintbox representation: almost surely each P_{t,ℓ} lies in (0,1), the sum over ℓ equals 1, and conditional on (P_{t,ℓ}) the partition Π(t) is generated by i.i.d. colors with distribution (P_{t,ℓ}).

The nearby self-similarity statement is Theorem 11: for each fixed t ≥ 0, the post-t forest grows by adding one leaf to one tree or adding a new root-only tree, and each component evolves as an independent copy of CTCS(n).
The subordinator must be specified exactly: Y_t := -log P_{t,1} is a subordinator with Lévy tail ψ∞[a,∞) = -log(1 - e^{-a}) and density f∞(a) = e^{-a}/(1 - e^{-a}) on (0,∞).

The equivalent transform identity must be stated if the question is to be self-contained: for t ≥ 0 and complex s with Re(s) > -1, E[P_{t,1}^s] = exp(-t(ψ(s+1) - ψ(1))), where ψ is the digamma function.

The exact/asymptotic distinction needs to be made explicit: for finite n, the harmonic descent chain is only approximated by the subordinator through log X_t^{(n)} ≈ log n - Y_t while Y_t < log n; the paper says this description becomes exact only in the n→∞ limit via P_{t,1}.

The consistency input creating the limit object must be included: Theorem 7 gives the delete-and-prune consistency of CTCS(n), and Proposition 1 gives the Exponential(1) branchpoint-height property that motivates the limiting branch decomposition.

No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree restriction, or nilpotency condition is relevant in this probabilistic setting; the missing details are instead the probabilistic objects, process parameters, ordering convention, and quantifiers t ≥ 0, ℓ ≥ 1, and n → ∞.
refined_question: Using the delete-and-prune consistency of the family (CTCS(n))_{n≥1}, formalize the limit object CTCS(∞) as the exchangeable partition process Π(t) of N obtained by cutting at height t; define the asymptotic clade frequencies P_{t,ℓ} = lim_{n→∞} |Π(t)_ℓ ∩ [n]|/n and prove the exact paintbox description of Π(t), the fixed-t self-similar forest decomposition, and the exact tagged-clade law Y_t := -log P_{t,1}, namely that (Y_t)_{t≥0} is the subordinator with Lévy tail ψ∞[a,∞) = -log(1 - e^{-a}) (equivalently E[P_{t,1}^s] = exp(-t(ψ(s+1) - ψ(1))) for all t ≥ 0 and Re(s) > -1)); in particular, make precise that the same subordinator appears for finite n only through the heuristic approximation of the harmonic descent chain, whereas it becomes exact only in the n→∞ limit.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, identify the tagged-clade frequency process (P_{t,1})_{t≥0} in CTCS(∞) by proving that for every t ≥ 0 and every complex s with Re(s) > -1, E[P_{t,1}^s] = exp(-t(ψ(s+1) - ψ(1))); this is exactly the statement that Y_t = -log P_{t,1} is the subordinator with Lévy density f∞(a) = e^{-a}/(1 - e^{-a}).
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper’s formalization of the infinite object and its tagged-branch process, but it introduces an external comparison object that the paper itself does not use. In the paper, CTCS(∞) is built from the consistency theorem (Theorem 7), formalized in Section 5.3 as an exchangeable partition process Π(t), described exactly by Kingman’s paintbox in Theorem 10, shown to satisfy a fixed-height self-similar forest decomposition in Theorem 11, and then equipped in Section 5.5 with the exact tagged-clade subordinator law in Theorem 12. By contrast, the same subordinator first appears earlier only as the finite-n approximation log X_t^{(n)} ≈ log n - Y_t for the harmonic descent chain. So the paper-faithful sharpening should ask for the exact exchangeable-partition/subordinator formalization of CTCS(∞) and for the precise exact-versus-asymptotic distinction internal to the paper, not for an external comparison with a beta(2,1) coalescent.
